# R63d34ce484: q_b0241d: Optimizer-Only Failure Audit (b0c328a25e046227be56a91508d0fe6756b416d3)
# q_b0241d: Optimizer-Only Failure Audit
## Conclusion
The original gold C is an ordinal full-recipe result, not a rate-only or mechanism result. Fresh controlled T2048 tests support its ordering on two allowed nested-oscillatory two-input analogues. At fixed AdamW betas(.9,.999) and wd1e-5, .001 beats3e-5 on both. This does not import K1081’s polynomial reversal or establish a T2048 rule. The proposed short-budget figures fail exact-model validation.
## Sources and Frozen Inputs
Before new training, reviewed K1081,K1088,K1103/K1104 and full Rb40ff6b901/R58d9d83b4f. Archived load_history (953 records),load_kb (64 claims),load_lab multivariate subset (3,761 rows),full q and prior reports. No persisted experiment was repeated; all previously experimented datasets were excluded from fresh selection.
q_b0241d: target `x0*x1+2*x1**2+sin(2*pi*cos(2*pi*x0)**2)`; two inputs,256 train/256 test uniform [0,1],point seed2085320852. Same default width256/depth3 plain LeakyReLU(.01),LN[T,F,T],MSE,T2048,batch16,32,768 samples. Gold C=AdamW(.001,wd.0001,betas.9/.95); B=AdamW(3e-5,wd1e-5,.9/.999); A=Adagrad(.003,wd.001). Prediction B was wrong. Gold reveals C beats both, not A/B ordering or original numerical effect sizes.
K1081 is fixed-beta2=.999 polynomial evidence on mvar_5a829e/93e6af; K1088 uses three-input w32/d5 residual SiLU/Adam. K1103/K1104 concern five-input w256/d5 residual models,batch32 and T256/1024. Their measured reversals constrain extrapolation; none ranks this target’s recipes. No parent claim was rewritten.
## Short-Budget Audit
Eligible pairs use one original,non-exp set_id; AdamW .001 versus Adagrad .003 or AdamW3e-5,identical budget and loss dictionaries. Exact model means full model-dictionary equality,not merely similar width or LN count. A win means lower aggregate test-MSE mean. Pair counts and set counts are separate; multiple pairs in one set are dependent. Finite means and zero failed seeds are separate filters.
| Contrast | Raw pairs / sets | Wins / ties | Finite pairs / sets | Nonexcluded zero-failure pairs / sets | Exact-model pairs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AdamW .001 vs Adagrad .003 |10 /8|9 /0|10 /8|10 /8|0|
| AdamW .001 vs AdamW3e-5 |11 /9|10 /1|5 /4|4 /3|0|
For Adagrad, both any-pair and all-pair set-win definitions yield7/8; therefore the nominal7/8 is reproducible only as a model-confounded set summary. The high/low AdamW audit gives8/9 winning sets,one nonfinite tie,not8/12. The missing denominator cannot be reconstructed from the frozen snapshot under these explicit filters. Neither number validates an optimizer-only matched-model conclusion.
Budget strata: Adagrad T256/batch16 (4,096 samples) has7/8 pair wins across6 sets; T512/batch16 (8,192 samples) has2/2 across2. Low AdamW at T256 has four clean finite pairs across3 sets,all high-rate wins; one finite pair with2 failed low-rate seeds also favors high; five nonfinite pairs across4 sets give four wins and one inf/inf tie. T512 has one high-finite/low-inf pair. There are no original-lab T2048 comparisons in these rate slices.
Data strata by input dimension, expressed pairs/sets: Adagrad dim2=2/2,dim3=1/1,dim4=3/3,dim5=4/2; low AdamW dim2=2/2,dim3=3/3,dim4=4/2,dim5=1/1,dim8=1/1. These mix targets and splits and cannot be pooled into a two-input nested-oscillatory rule.
Applying the proposed scope to BOTH candidates (width≥128,at least one LN,plain MSE,oscillatory sin/cos target,4,096–8,192 samples) leaves only one Adagrad comparison and no low-AdamW comparison. That pair,mvar_c966f7/set_4096_var_var_fix_e0972b,c_be0d13 versus c_612c99,changes model and favors Adagrad: AdamW .02240767 versus .01743076,difference+.00497692,ratio1.28553.
Historical finite AdamW-minus-Adagrad effects span−.50226485 to+.00497692; ratios .01586–1.28553. All ten pairs have zero reported failures. Finite high-minus-low AdamW effects span−.85689695 to−.02481959; ratios .00779–.93699. Four are clean; mvar_f489a0 has2 failed low-rate seeds despite a finite aggregate. Complete candidate-level effects,expressions,budgets and failure counts are in historical_effects.csv.
Nonfinite low-rate strata are retained: mvar_2e1d28 has10 failed seeds on BOTH recipes; mvar_3cf8f5,54e3a3,5e9d75(two pairs),afd61d each have10 failed low-rate seeds and0 high-rate failures. Their infinite endpoints are not numerical effect sizes or ordinary optimization wins. This substantially weakens any pooled success-rate interpretation.
## Preregistration and Methods
Published R63d34ce484 before outcomes,commit6b38e7e0e03f38617d901612e18fd8dc0f1bce20. Selected the first two lexicographic fresh allowed two-input datasets with nested oscillation,excluding every dataset in a persisted exp: set. Both have256 train/test uniform [0,1] points and both inputs active.
mvar_0eb811: instance30092028,point30093028,target `x0*x1**3+cos(2*pi*x0)**2+tanh(2*cos(2*pi*sin(2*pi*x1)))`. mvar_133302: instance51092094,point51093094,target `x1**3+x0*x1+cos(2*pi*sin(2*pi*x0))`. Target and split change jointly,so their differences cannot isolate expression complexity.
Each dataset received one joint six-variant experiment at T2048,batch16 (32,768 samples;128 nominal train exposures),with q’s model/default initialization/plain MSE. G,L,A are q’s gold,low and Adagrad recipes. H=AdamW(.001,wd1e-5,.9/.999); F=AdamW(.001,wd1e-5,.9/.95); S=AdamW(3e-5,wd1e-5,.9/.95). H/L and F/S isolate rate conditional on beta; F/H and S/L isolate beta2 conditional on rate; G/F isolates decay at high rate/beta2=.95. Adagrad remains a full-recipe contrast,not an algorithm-only comparison.
Before outcomes predicted G beats L and A on both; H beats L and F beats S on both; F beats H on both. Low-rate beta and decay directions were left unresolved. All directional predictions succeeded; the unresolved contrasts are reported,not retroactively predicted. No T256 experiment was run: no reversal was observed requiring a crossover search,and no crossover location is claimed.
Resolved records confirm identical model dictionaries,LeakyReLU slope.01 (canonical leaky_relu_slope plus submitted alias),plain mse without a regularizer,and exact budgets. Adagrad has no active Adam betas. Initialization convention is fixed,not proof of identical weights or minibatch streams across cells.
## New Results
Mean held-out MSE ± seed SD; ten-seed protocol per cell. E1=exp:84c99dbb5600,E2=exp:dfcd5d3d248c; all effects compare within these sets.
| Dataset | G | L | A | H | F | S |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|0eb811|.174114±.069100|.410492±.027387|.243132±.046913|.186572±.072636|.163248±.068218|.443201±.033739|
|133302|.051493±.024047|.298363±.016580|.234144±.033448|.064905±.037385|.053575±.019577|.316919±.011190|
| Contrast (first minus / divided by second) | E1 difference / ratio | E2 difference / ratio |
|---|---:|---:|
|G−L / G:L|−.23637771 /.42416|−.24687081 /.17258|
|G−A / G:A|−.06901775 /.71613|−.18265095 /.21992|
|H−L / H:L,rate beta2=.999|−.22391917 /.45451|−.23345834 /.21754|
|F−S / F:S,rate beta2=.95|−.27995368 /.36834|−.26334396 /.16905|
|F−H / F:H,beta high-rate|−.02332461 /.87498|−.01133009 /.82544|
|S−L / S:L,beta low-rate|+.03270991 /1.07968|+.01855553 /1.06219|
|G−F / G:F,decay|+.01086607 /1.06656|−.00208238 /.96113|
Gold wins2/2 versus each full recipe. Higher rate wins2/2 at each beta. Beta2=.95 improves high-rate endpoints but worsens low-rate endpoints2/2,a counterexample to unconditional “faster beta adaptation helps.” Higher decay hurts E1 and helps E2; no uniform decay benefit follows. Full-recipe superiority cannot be assigned solely to beta or decay.
effects.csv also reports descriptive standardized differences using sqrt((SD_a²+SD_b²)/2): rate999 −4.079/−8.073; rate95 −5.202/−16.516; beta-high −.331/−.380; beta-low1.065/1.312; decay .158/−.095. These are dispersion-scaled effects,not paired statistical tests or calibrated population probabilities. Small beta/decay differences relative to high-rate dispersion deserve particular caution.
All12 aggregates are finite and all12 immediate result cells report error=null. Protocol n=10 is not a recovered finite-seed count: finite and failed seed counts,individual losses,paired covariance and paired-win rates are unavailable and preserved as null in effects artifacts. SD is not a confidence interval. Fourteen derived contrasts do not represent14 independent experiments,and the two datasets are not a random population sample.
## Mechanisms and Distinguishing Tests
Endpoint test MSE supports local recipe/rate order,not undertraining,overfitting,sustained adaptive motion or Adagrad accumulator suppression. Rate changes may alter fitting speed,trajectory/basin,update noise and rate-scaled decay; even matched decay coefficients imply unequal cumulative AdamW shrinkage. Beta/decay sensitivity is measured locally,not a mechanistic decomposition of all interactions.
Unexecuted predictions: a fitting-limited low-rate account predicts poorer training MSE at3e-5 as well as poorer test MSE; equal/better low-rate training fit would weaken it. Overfitting predicts improved training loss alongside worsening held-out loss,requiring repeated paired train/test checkpoints rather than separate endpoints. A sustained-update account predicts larger useful measured parameter updates for high-rate AdamW late in training; losses alone cannot test it.
An Adagrad-accumulator account predicts a controlled state-reset intervention changes late progress,with weight/batch/rate controls. A beta-memory account predicts preserved-versus-reset moment or fixed-beta interventions change trajectories beyond early transient effects. These need instrumentation/state forks not exposed by the documented endpoint interface; no unsupported schedules or keys were guessed.
## Checkpoint, Scope and Reproduction
refresh_observations pinned J415ee88e142a_research_e0003:923 history records,66 claims,11,533 lab rows. No question IDs were added;30 initial records including q were absent. Frozen q is retained rather than treating omission as retraction. Previously archived measured rows present in the refresh have unchanged mean,SD and failure counts. Both views are saved;refresh is not independent corroboration.
No polynomial result was pooled with these nested-oscillatory tests. Original short budgets remain separate from T2048. No universal ceiling,optimizer ranking,continuous optimum,budget threshold or generalization mechanism follows. New splits,the original q split,other nested targets,width/LN/activation/init/batch changes,optimizer defaults and budgets beyond T2048 remain unresolved.
optimizer_audit contains frozen history/KB/lab,question,prior sources,selection,pairs,new resolved records,checkpoint and analyze.py. Running `python optimizer_audit/analyze.py` regenerates historical_effects.csv and effects.json/csv,checks12 cells,identical models/plain loss/budgets,and recomputes14 same-set contrasts. It was executed successfully via the Python sandbox with its script path bound explicitly after an initial execution-wrapper path error; no training was repeated to fix that analysis error.
Added only **K1105**,506 characters,limited to the fixed-beta/decay rate result on these two datasets. No parent edits or general ceiling. Published **R63d34ce484**,latest commit `c784eafddb94a16fe5df85a087e119fe179308a3`. This report is independently reviewable measurement evidence,not a finished theory.

# R7dd7d943d3: Displacement over-selection: controlled progress and late-precision audit (4b55a660e0615effa0770f7a78e6aac418dadeb7)
# Displacement Over-Selection: Progress, Precision and Failed Metrics

## Evidence and Definitions
Frozen inputs: 863 visible training records, 35 KB claims and 11,215 lab candidates. Only visible training answers and within-set allowed-lab measurements were used. Checkpoint refresh repinned `Jbb8de54d2489_research_e0001`; no new history records appeared.

Nominal displacement Δ is a progress proxy, not measured parameter movement: adaptive optimizers use `lr·T`; Adagrad uses `2·lr·√T`; SGD uses `lr·T·g/(1−m)` with assumed gradient scales. Architecture, target scale and optimizer state can invalidate those approximations. Late precision means a smaller rate beats a larger rate at the **same budget**, not merely that longer training worsens loss.

Training answers provide ordinal outcomes, not loss ratios. Lab results are ten-seed means and seed standard deviations, not confidence intervals. Pair counts share candidates and are dependent. No significance, seed-win frequency or causal overconfidence claim is inferred.

## Frozen Audit
Exact matching of dataset/set, model, loss, budget and all optimizer settings except learning rate found only **3 pairs across 3 sets**, all bigram LM. Higher rate won all three:
- Width-64/depth-2 GRU, AdamW, `.0003→.003`, 256 steps/batch32: loss ratio **0.92163**.
- Width-32/depth-3 transformer, RMSprop, `.0001→.0003`, 256/batch16: **0.98532**.
- Width-64/depth-1 GRU, plain SGD, `.001→.003`, 256/batch32: **0.99909**.

Broader same-model/loss/budget comparisons with ≥3× nominal-Δ gaps also vary optimizer, decay or betas. They describe progress evidence, not isolated rate effects:

| Family | Higher-Δ wins/pairs | Sets | Budget strata | Median high/low loss |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| Univariate MSE | 12/13 | 13 | 256/b16 | .1273 |
| Multivariate MSE | 9/9 | 9 | 256/b16 | .4610 |
| Tabular CE | 45/48 | 18 | 256/b16:23/23; 256/b32:22/25 | .4272 |
| Bigram CE | 53/57 | 5 | 256/b16:1/1; 256/b32:41/44; 512/b16:11/12 | .9336 |
| Spiral CE | 14/14 | 14 | 256/b16:12/12; 256/b32:2/2 | .7833 |
| XOR CE | 19/19 | 19 | 256/b16:18/18; 256/b32:1/1 | .4019 |

Counterexamples remain in the artifacts: width-24/depth-3 univariate Adam versus AdamW gives high/low MSE **1.3477**; three width-128/depth-6 tabular comparisons give **1.0201, 1.0973, 1.0757**; four bigram comparisons give **1.0005, 1.0098, 1.0007, 1.0228**. These are optimizer-confounded, sometimes near-ties. Original spiral/XOR labs had no 2048-step comparisons.

## Controlled Results
All comparisons below are within their named experiment sets. Batch16 is fixed; 256/2048 steps correspond to 4096/32768 sampled rows. Each experiment uses an allowed lab split, **not the original failure-question split**. Exact data cards, candidate IDs, resolved recipes and seed SDs are archived.

**Univariate, `sym_0c2620`, `exp:34aa6df219ff`.** Target `cos(2π·cos(2πx))−1`; width128/depth2, nonresidual LeakyReLU(.01), no LayerNorm, Adam(.9,.95), decay1e-5. At 2048 steps, rates `.00003/.0001/.0003/.003` give MSE **.52273/.35314/.27677/.01578**, SD **.00624/.02743/.01039/.01092**. Higher rates win **6/6** grid pairs. Rate `.003`, Δ=6.144, beats all three lower rates with ratios **.0302/.0447/.0570**. The preregistered overshoot-penalty prediction was falsified.

**Multivariate, `mvar_000e80`, `exp:46dafe43cf05`.** Three-input oscillatory target; width32/depth5 residual SiLU, LN `[F,F,T,F,T]`, Adam(.9,.999), decay1e-4. Rates `.0003/.003` give MSE **.77893±.20585 versus .69733±.06546** at256, then **.65152±.02806 versus .70482±.04937** at2048. Higher rate wins **1/2**; ratios **.8952 then 1.0818**. The prediction that high rate wins both budgets failed.

**Smooth tabular, `stabcls_021b60`, `exp:e3b7925d9c02`.** Eight features, 1024 train rows; width256/depth1 nonresidual ReLU+LN, Adam(.9,.999), decay1e-4. Rates `.00003/.0003/.001` give CE **.41170/.22133/.18960** at256 and **.22041/.14817/.16338** at2048. Higher rates win **3/3 short, 2/3 long**. The `.001/.0003` ratio reverses **.8566→1.1026**, but `.001` still beats `.00003`. Best tested long-budget Δ is **.6144**, not .05–.15. This is a grid minimum, not a continuous optimum.

**Bigram, `bg_013a4e`, `exp:88b5f9940c28`.** V32/context16, transformer width32/depth4/heads4/FF128, Adam(.9,.999), decay0, CE+L1(.01). Rates `.0003/.003` give CE **3.07942±.01672 versus 2.90496±.01020** at256, ratio **.9433**. At2048, `.0003` gives **2.96067±.01045**; `.003` returns mean/std **Infinity**, with `error=null`. This is a failed metric, not measured overconfidence or a known 10/10 seed failure. The failure boundary between rates is unmeasured.

**Spiral, `spiralcls_0516f4`, `exp:3dbc82fbb876`.** 1.5 turns; width256/depth2 residual SiLU, two LN, Adam(.9,.95). At decay1e-5, rates `.0001/.001` give CE **.38286±.02921 versus .002943±.002527** at256, then **1.4944e-5±6.6274e-6 versus 1.7412e-5±1.9878e-5** at2048. Ratios reverse **.00769→1.1651**. At2048/decay1e-4, the lower rate again wins by mean, ratio **1.0207**. Higher rate wins **1/1 short, 0/2 long**, but tiny losses and overlapping SDs preclude a confident general ceiling. Higher decay raises mean CE **8.209×/7.192×** at the two rates.

An exploratory AdamW spiral grid, `exp:b7eb3f31d314`, favored `.003` over `.0003` at256 but reached **0 versus 2.4267e-8** at2048. The ratio is undefined at this numerical floor. It is not persuasive late-precision evidence and is not merged with Adam.

**XOR rate-only, `xorcls_0dd7d2`, `exp:d82786f1e971`.** Sixteen features; width24/depth3 nonresidual GELU, LN `[T,F,T]`, AdamW(.9,.95), decay0. Rates `.0001/.001/.003` give CE **.68965/.49647/.28717** at256 and **.52577/.39903/.32104** at2048. Higher rates win **all six** grid pairs. The predicted low-rate reversal failed. Rate `.003` nevertheless worsens **1.1179×** with more steps; deterioration does not imply that a lower rate wins at2048.

**XOR optimizer contrast, joint set `exp:1ea73c34d11a`.** Same data/network, lr.001/decay0: AdamW versus momentum-SGD(.9) gives CE **.49647±.05247 versus .68676±.00540** at256 and **.39903±.06612 versus .23307±.03458** at2048. AdamW/SGD ratios reverse **.7229→1.7120**, despite nominal AdamW Δ being10× larger. SGD decay.001 gives **.22954±.03241**, only .98483× the decay0 mean. Separate pilots were repeated together; final evidence is within this joint set.

## Failure and KB Audit
- **q_af3ba4:** gold `E<C<B<A<D`, predicted `E<B<A<D<C`. Nominal Δ(E,C,B,A,D)=`.6144,6.144,.2048,.06144,.02715`. C loses only to E, not to slower rivals. Optimizer/betas/decay also vary; history does not isolate fine-fitting. New controlled univariate evidence defeats an absolute high-Δ cutoff.
- **q_7a5eba:** gold `A<D<C<B<E`, predicted `D<A<C<B<E`. At E=16, A’s width32/depth3/one-LN LeakyReLU AdamW Δ=.256 beats D’s width24/depth5/three-LN GELU RMSprop Δ=.0768. A same-network sweet spot cannot determine this cross-architecture ordering.
- **q_09b159:** gold B, predicted A. Adagrad A has nominal Δ=.2715; differently shaped plain-SGD B has .06144 under the assumed gradient scale. **q_94ff32 has identical candidate bullets on another target and favors A.** Offset-memory and gradient-preservation explanations remain unmeasured.
- **q_46d72e:** gold `E<A<B<C<D`, predicted `B<A<E<D<C`. New joint XOR evidence supports the long-budget SGD/AdamW contrast on one other split, but rate-only AdamW evidence rejects a general low-rate explanation. The complete gold ordering remains unvalidated.
- **q_fb4a7f:** A is Adam.0001/decay1e-5; B Adam.001/decay1e-4; C AdamW.00003/decay0. New Adam checks separate a tiny rate effect from a larger decay-associated change on the lab split; neither establishes the original failure’s cause.

At input, K1001 asserted universal undertraining and monotonic ranking; K1012 combined gap-based ranking with saturation caveats. At refresh, both first sentences were already corrected to conditional progress and uncertain comparisons. Those edits were preserved. K1072 now correctly rejects automatic last-place overshoot. K1073 now rejects cross-architecture reversal, but its numeric optima still need explicit dataset/recipe/batch scope. Inherited KB counts were not treated as newly verified rate-only denominators.

## Claims and Falsifiers
Six conditional factual claims, each ≤700 characters, were submitted as **K1076–K1081**, plus annotations to K1072/K1073. Exact texts are in `proposed_claims.json`.

They record the univariate high-Δ counterexample; tabular and multivariate budget reversals; bigram nonfinite output; weak spiral mean reversal; and XOR’s separation of optimizer reversal from rate-only progress.

An exact same-split/recipe/seeds0–9 recomputation that fails the stated inequalities falsifies each measured claim. A finite recomputation of bigram `.003/2048`, or a demonstrated reporting artifact, falsifies its failure statement. New splits or seed cohorts can falsify predictive extensions, but are not contradictions of recorded measurements. No family-wide threshold is proposed.

## Explanations and Boundaries
Late refinement, optimizer-specific trajectories, regularization and numerical instability compete with overconfidence/distractor fitting. The latter requires train/test CE, logit norms and confidence on errors, none measured here. MSE reversals cannot be called logit overconfidence.

Unrun, distinguishable predictions: confident-error inflation should lower train CE while raising held-out confidence on errors; numerical instability should respond to smaller rates or clipping; an offset-memory explanation should alter Adagrad accumulators and ordering on architecture-matched offset interventions. These are tests to perform, not established mechanisms.

Thresholds remain grid-local: tabular Δ=.6144 beats .06144 and2.048; univariate6.144 can beat .2048; one bigram transformer/L1 recipe is finite at `.0003` and nonfinite at `.003` after2048 steps. No universal cutoff, width law, batch law or extrapolation from256 to2048 follows. Five selected failures cannot quantify population-wide solver bias.

## Reproducibility
Published report **R7dd7d943d3**, commit **c0215f89f6ea98b7178b314456ee484c0e167f45**. The committed `displacement_audit` directory preserves frozen inputs/provenance, predictions, raw responses, exact experiment rows and analysis. Run `python displacement_audit/analyze.py` to recompute strict pairs, proxy pairs, budget strata and nonfinite flags.

The audit is independently reviewable, not a finished mechanism theory. Remaining uncertainties include paired-seed inference, cross-split/width transfer, batch effects, continuous thresholds, and calibration versus optimization causes.

# Rb40ff6b901: Polynomial AdamW reversal: report-only mechanism audit (9d3c0ad9072c184d44fc17aa205f296ee04baf73)
# Polynomial AdamW Reversal: Mechanism Audit
Published **Rb40ff6b901**, commit `a8fc49cf315478c182c97f00ffbf6f1631995734`. Report-only: no claims added, rewritten or deleted; no counts reset; no training experiments repeated.

## Evidence and Scope
Read the latest visible Rc5401dd3c0 and R7dd7d943d3 and requested K1080/K1081. Initial frozen inputs contained 893 history records, 37 claims and 11,366 lab candidates. A checkpoint refresh pinned `J327e1059d773_research_e0002`, exposing 893 records, 59 claims and 11,449 candidates. All 20 records for the two focal polynomial datasets remained unchanged.

There is an identifier discrepancy: `kb_open` resolves K1080/K1081 to the polynomial/oscillatory claims, while refreshed `load_kb` assigns those texts K1081/K1088. Both views are archived; neither was edited. Evidence below is identified by experiment and dataset.

Only visible training history and allowed lab records were used. Historical `q_38909f` favors low-rate AdamW, but its high-rate rival also changes decay and beta2. Its ordinal answer does not isolate learning rate.

## Fixed Recipe
Two-input, nonresidual MLP: width256/depth3, LeakyReLU(.01), pre-linear LayerNorm pattern `[1,0,1]`, default initialization, AdamW betas(.9,.999), wd1e-5, batch16. Primary objective is **plain MSE**, comparing lr3e-5 with .001.

Both datasets have 256 train/256 test rows and domain `[0,1]`. Targets are `x0**3+x0*x1+x1-2` on `mvar_5a829e` and `x0*x1**2+x1**3+x0` on `mvar_93e6af`. Target and split change jointly between datasets.

T256/T2048 correspond to 4,096/32,768 sampled rows, or 16/128 nominal exposure epochs. Update count and exposure therefore co-vary. Initialization convention is fixed, but actual paired weights and minibatch streams cannot be verified from aggregates. Equal AdamW decay also does not imply equal cumulative shrinkage, because decay is rate-scaled.

## Results
| Dataset / T / objective | Low mean ± SD | High mean ± SD | High/low |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 5a829e /256 /plain MSE | .00521305 ± .00091476 | .00091443 ± .00024744 | .17541 |
| 5a829e /2048 /plain MSE | .00060866 ± .00007366 | .00143579 ± .00068928 | 2.35895 |
| 93e6af /2048 /plain MSE | .00003166 ± .00002056 | .00397847 ± .00885354 | 125.67780 |
| 5a829e /256 /accidental MSE+L2(.001) | .00521236 ± .00091460 | .00092862 ± .00024596 | .17816 |
| 5a829e /2048 /accidental MSE+L2(.001) | .00060267 ± .00007457 | .00217262 ± .00161909 | 3.60498 |

Primary sources are `exp:630c92c3db03` and `exp:ab716597e66e`. The original inherited-loss protocol error, `exp:585913a8fe26`, remains supplementary; it is neither pooled with nor relabeled as plain MSE.

Low rate wins **2/2 datasets at T2048**. On 5a829e, high rate wins at T256 but loses at T2048. These are fresh-run endpoints, not a measured continuation trajectory. The crossover location remains unknown.

High-rate SD on 93e6af exceeds its mean; CV is 2.22536. Conditional on ten finite, nonnegative seed losses all contributing, the moments imply at least one endpoint ≥.02171059 using sample SD, or ≥.02368083 using population SD. This is a mathematical bound, not a recovered measurement. It establishes heterogeneity, **not divergence, outlier count, median ordering, paired seed wins or calibrated future-seed probability**.

## Tool Limitations
The exposed training interface documents fresh base-plus-override comparisons returning ten-seed selection-metric means/SDs. It exposes no documented seed selection, initial metrics, training MSE, trajectories, checkpoint continuation, optimizer-state reset or schedules. Resource/template listings are empty.

Some original-lab records contain failure/exclusion fields, but the focal experiment records do not. Their absence is not evidence that every seed remained stable. Unsupported capabilities may exist internally, but are unavailable through the inspected interface.

No new training was run. Additional endpoint grids would not identify the requested train-fit versus generalization versus excursion signatures. Guessed intervention keys would not constitute controlled measurements.

## Preregistered Discriminators
1. **Reversible late precision:** at T1024, fork identical weights, batches and preserved Adam state into 512 further updates at .001 versus3e-5. Log full-train and fixed-test MSE every32 steps. Predict downshift reduces both residuals in stable seeds. Persistent failure to improve training fit, or test-only improvement with worse training fit, weakens this reversible precision-floor explanation.

2. **Tail-dominant instability:** first retrieve original per-seed endpoints and trajectories, including finite flags and gradient/update norms. Predict poor high-rate seeds exhibit training excursions or sustained fitting failure, and paired downshift rescues them. Stable equal/better training with a broad median test disadvantage weakens this explanation. Schedule rescue alone cannot distinguish instability from precision.

3. **Generalization-dominant reversal:** compare paired train/test MSE at matched checkpoint ages. Predict high rate achieves equal/better training fit while test loss and the generalization gap worsen. Worse train and test together, followed by improvement of both after downshift, contradicts a pure generalization-only account. Mixed mechanisms remain possible.

4. **Optimizer-state dependence:** use a T1024 2×2 fork: low/high continuation rate crossed with preserving/resetting moments and step counter, while retaining weights and batches. A sustained reset effect supports state sensitivity; no sustained effect weakens state-memory dominance. Reset is not a pure beta2 intervention.

These tests are **preregistered but unexecuted**, because the necessary instrumentation and interventions are not exposed.

## Predictions and Boundaries
A stochastic late-step noise-floor explanation predicts that increasing batch16→64 attenuates the high-rate disadvantage when sufficient updates permit fitting. Future batch64 pairs at T512 and T2048 separate matched-exposure from matched-update comparisons. Lack of attenuation weakens that extension; one batch contrast alone cannot settle the mechanism.

A simple reversible refinement explanation predicts a T1024 high-to-low switch improves train/test fit relative to high-rate continuation. It need not beat fixed low-rate training because earlier trajectories may enter different basins. Failure to recover weakens the reversible-floor account while leaving irreversible path dependence open.

Independent splits with unchanged expression are needed to separate target from data effects. Width, initialization, batch order, beta2, decay and normalization require separately controlled interventions. No direction of width transfer is established here.

The oscillatory Adam reversal and prior high-rate counterexamples prevent a universal multivariate low-rate ceiling. Neither a continuous optimum, an epoch cutoff nor seed-success probability follows from these polynomial aggregates.

## Reproducibility
`mechanism_audit/` preserves source reports, both claim views, relevant history, all20 focal records, checkpoint manifests, preregistration, analysis code and computed results. `python mechanism_audit/analyze.py` verifies within-set controls and recomputes ratios, margins, CVs and conditional moment bounds without rerunning training.

**Conclusion:** the budget reversal is measured; its cause remains unidentified. Paired train/test trajectories and per-seed observations would distinguish late fitting precision, tail instability and generalization. This report is independently reviewable, not a finished mechanism theory.

# Same-Architecture Long-Budget Rate Audit

## Evidence and Scope
Read R7dd7d943d3 and current KB first; preserved their survived repairs and did not rerun existing experiments. Initial inputs were 893 visible training records and 11,366 lab candidates, including prior experiments. Only visible training history and allowed lab measurements were used; no evaluation-answer files were accessed.

The checkpoint refresh pinned e0001: 863 records, no new question IDs, and updated KB repairs. Initial e0002 inputs remain archived. This refresh supplied no later training evidence.

The supplied epoch-2 higher/lower-log-Delta counts motivate this investigation but were not independently reconstructed as population-bias statistics. Selected failures and outcome-selected dataflip records cannot establish universal error frequencies.

Nominal Δ is an optimizer-based progress proxy, not measured parameter movement. Ratios below are high-rate mean held-out loss divided by low-rate mean; margins are high minus low. Standard deviations describe ten training seeds, not paired confidence intervals.

## Training and Lab Audit
**q_38909f:** dimension-2 polynomial `x0*x1**2+x0**3+x1**2+.5`; 256 train/256 test points; T2048, batch16, 32768 samples. Shared default-init nonresidual depth3/width256 LeakyReLU(.01) MLP, LN `[T,F,T]`. Winning AdamW B uses lr3e-5, wd1e-5, betas(.9,.999); losing AdamW C uses lr.001, wd1e-4, betas(.9,.95). This is same architecture, not rate-only. History provides no numerical margins.

**q_a57013:** dimension16 piecewise classification; 1024 train/2048 test rows; T512, batch64, 32768 samples, or 32 exposure epochs. Shared default-init nonresidual depth4/width256 GELU, LN `[T,F,T,F]`. Observed order is RMSprop(3e-5,wd.001) < Adagrad(.0001,wd.001) < Adagrad(.003,wd1e-5) < AdamW(.0003,wd1e-5) < SGD. Even the Adagrad comparison changes decay. “Generalization reversal” remains an explanation to test, not a measured mechanism.

Visible-history same-architecture/same-optimizer comparisons favor higher rate in **38/45 comparisons across28 questions** for multivariate regression and **31/34 across19** for tabular classification. Equal displayed optimizer settings except rate reduce these to **4/5 across5** and **8/10 across10**, respectively. These dependent comparisons include imported visible training records.

The original lab has **zero rate-only pairs/zero sets** in these families under exact within-set model, initialization, loss, optimizer-config and budget matching. Existing controlled experiments were retained separately.

## Preregistration and Controls
Predictions were recorded before outcomes: polynomial high-rate wins short/low-rate wins long; deep-GELU Adagrad likewise reverses at 32 exposure epochs; polynomial reversal transfers to another polynomial; historical sparse/smooth AdamW reversal transfers to lab analogues; RMSprop beats AdamW in a full-recipe tabular analogue.

Each rate pair fixes dataset, architecture, width, normalization, initialization convention, loss, optimizer configuration and budget. All runs start fresh. Across budgets, batch remains fixed but T and samples seen change together: their separate effects are unidentified.

A protocol error is preserved: the first polynomial experiment inherited MSE+L2(.001), rather than preregistered plain MSE. A separately identified plain-MSE control corrected this. The inherited-loss results are supplementary, not substituted for the intended test.

Unspecified optimizer knobs use runner defaults; optimizer-state trajectories were not independently measured.

## Full-Recipe and Dataset Reversals
Within `exp:ddb38c8f1249`, the deep-GELU architecture on piecewise `stabcls_06550f`, T512/batch64, gives:

AdamW/RMSprop ratio is **1.23759**, margin **+.069321**, from **1 comparison/1 set**. This transports one full-recipe reversal from q_a57013, without identifying rate, decay or optimizer state as its cause. Higher nominal Δ wins only **1/3 optimizer-pair comparisons** in this set.

The preregistered reuse of a slow-Adagrad cell from another experiment is inadmissible under within-set comparison rules; no cross-set E/C numerical ratio is used.

Two exact-recipe historical dataset reversals remain relevant:
- **q_a9073c/q_07b812:** dimension8 residual ReLU depth2/width192, LN `[F,T]`, AdamW, rates.001/3e-5, T1024/batch32. Higher wins sparse; lower wins smooth.
- **q_9d6507/q_b9d45e:** dimension8 nonresidual ReLU depth1/width192, no LN, RMSprop wd0, rates.001/.0001, same budget. Higher wins sparse; lower wins smooth.

These are **2 matched recipe groups/4 question sets**, with ordinal outcomes and unavailable numerical margins. Rule family, active features, coefficients and split seeds change jointly. Controlled W analogues do not reproduce the first reversal: both favor higher rate. Historical counterexamples stand, but family labels alone do not transport their ordering.

## Interpretation and Unresolved Tests
Short-budget high-rate wins are compatible with progress limitation. Long-budget reversals remain compatible with late precision, instability, optimizer-specific trajectories or generalization. Endpoint losses alone distinguish none of these mechanisms.

Discriminating tests remain unrun: collect training/test trajectories; compare high-to-low schedules against fixed-rate controls at equal samples; compare continuation with preserved versus reset optimizer state; cross batch sizes under separately matched T and samples; measure finite-loss failures and clipping responses. Falling training loss with rising test loss would favor generalization over failure to fit.

No continuous optimum, universal epoch cutoff, dimension/width law or population-wide bias mechanism follows. Original question splits, alternative initializations, independent seed cohorts and intermediate rates remain untested. Multivariate exclusion from univariate overshoot is not evidence of high-rate safety.

## Publication and Reproducibility

Published **Rc5401dd3c0**, commit **1e459f265c35bb1e2ef32bb4a161b0a85ee538d3**. This report is independently reviewable, but unfinished as a mechanism theory.
